intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that spermatogenic failure-103 (SPGF103) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the MEI1 gene on chromosome 22q13.

checks.claim: Spermatogenic failure-103 (SPGF103) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the MEI1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Ben Khelifa and his team used WES technology to screen and identify a homozygous missense mutation c.C3307T (p.Arg1103Trp) in the MEI1 among two infertile brothers from a consanguineous Tunisian family
checks.explanation: The paper reports compound heterozygous MEI1 mutations and cites earlier homozygous cases, but it never uses the disease name SPGF103 and does not formally state the causal claim at this level.

checks.claim: The MEI1 gene is located on chromosome 22q13.
checks.evidence_quote: revealed the location of MEI1 in chromosome 22 (22q13.2)
checks.explanation: The paper places MEI1 at 22q13.2, which matches 22q13.

paragraphs.text: Spermatogenic failure-103 (SPGF103) is an autosomal recessive form of male infertility. Affected men have nonobstructive azoospermia with spermatogenesis arrested at the spermatocyte stage, or cryptozoospermia (Chen et al., 2023; Zhang et al., 2023; Liu et al., 2025).

checks.claim: Spermatogenic failure-103 (SPGF103) is an autosomal recessive form of male infertility.
checks.evidence_quote: The mutations were inherited from their parents, who were both single heterozygous carriers, indicating a recessive pattern of inheritance.
checks.explanation: The paper describes recessive inheritance. MEI1 is on chromosome 22, so the inheritance is autosomal.

checks.claim: Men affected with SPGF103 have nonobstructive azoospermia with spermatogenesis arrested at the spermatocyte stage, or cryptozoospermia.
checks.evidence_quote: which was the first report of nonobstructive azoospermia (NOA) caused by MEI1 gene mutation due to meiotic arrest
checks.explanation: The paper describes NOA from meiotic arrest (in a cited study) and cryptozoospermia (in this family). Arrest at the spermatocyte stage is described only in knockout mice.

paragraphs.text: Chen et al. (2023) reported 2 Chinese brothers with infertility. The proband was a 30-year-old man who had been infertile for 5 years. He had normal external genitalia, bilateral testicular volumes of about 12 ml, and nothing abnormal on palpation of the spermatic cords or vasa deferentia. Semen volume and pH were normal. No spermatozoa were seen in the initial semen smear, but a smear of centrifuged sediment showed 0 to 1 sperm per high-power field, consistent with cryptozoospermia. A total of 10 to 15 spermatozoa were found in 20 high-power fields; 2 to 3 were progressively motile and 2 to 3 had normal morphology. Serum FSH, LH, testosterone, estradiol, prolactin, thyrotropin, ACTH, inhibin B, and anti-Mullerian hormone were all normal. He had a 46,XY karyotype and no AZF microdeletions of the Y chromosome. His brother had been infertile through 3 years of marriage and also had cryptozoospermia, with occasional motile sperm (0 to 1) seen only after semen centrifugation. Physical examination and laboratory tests were otherwise unremarkable in the brother.

paragraphs.text: Malcher et al. (2022) performed whole-genome sequencing in 39 men with various types of nonobstructive azoospermia. In 1 patient they identified compound heterozygous variants in the MEI1 gene: c.1546A-G, resulting in an ile516-to-val (I516V) substitution, and c.3542G-A, resulting in an arg1181-to-gln (R1181Q) substitution. The authors listed MEI1 among genes previously associated with infertility in which they had found potential NOA-associated variants. No segregation or functional data were reported.

paragraphs.text: In 2 Chinese brothers with cryptozoospermia, Chen et al. (2023) used whole-exome sequencing of the proband to identify compound heterozygous mutations in the MEI1 gene. One was a splicing mutation (c.529+5G-A) downstream of exon 5, and the other was a missense mutation (c.2071C-G) in exon 18 resulting in a gln691-to-glu (Q691E) substitution. Sanger sequencing confirmed the mutations in both brothers. The father, who had normal fertility, was heterozygous for c.2071C-G, and the mother was heterozygous for c.529+5G-A. Neither variant was found in the ExAC or gnomAD databases. The splicing mutation was predicted to affect splicing, and the missense mutation was predicted to be deleterious by several in silico tools. Because sperm were extremely scarce and testicular tissue was not available, MEI1 mRNA and protein could not be studied. The authors suggested that the combination of the 2 mutations might allow slight MEI1 expression and occasional completion of meiosis, which would explain cryptozoospermia rather than azoospermia.

checks.explanation: WES was done on the proband and identified a compound heterozygous MEI1 mutation in the brothers with cryptozoospermia.

checks.explanation: The missense variant is c.2071C>G (p.Gln691Glu) in exon 18.

paragraphs.text: In 4 Chinese patients with nonobstructive azoospermia, Zhang et al. (2023) used whole-exome sequencing to identify biallelic deleterious variants in the MEI1 gene. In vitro, a missense variant (c.186G-C) reduced MEI1 expression and a frameshift variant (c.251delT) produced truncated MEI1 proteins. Bioinformatic analysis suggested that another missense variant (c.1585T-A) affected the interaction of MEI1 with its partners.

paragraphs.text: In a man with azoospermia and a woman with embryonic arrest from a consanguineous family, Liu et al. (2025) used whole-exome sequencing to identify a homozygous deletion of the whole of exon 19 of the MEI1 gene, which they confirmed by Sanger sequencing. Their mother was a heterozygous carrier. Sequencing of cDNA confirmed loss of exon 19, and quantitative analysis showed almost no detectable expression of exon 19 in the patients. When the mutant was transfected into HEK293T cells, Western blotting showed a truncated MEI1 protein, consistent with the predicted premature termination in exon 20.

paragraphs.text: In 2 Chinese brothers with cryptozoospermia (SPGF103), Chen et al. The mutations were found by whole-exome sequencing and confirmed by Sanger sequencing. The mother was heterozygous for the c.529+5G-A mutation and the father was heterozygous for the Q691E mutation. Neither variant was present in the ExAC or gnomAD databases.

paragraphs.text: In a man with azoospermia (SPGF103) and a woman with embryonic arrest from a consanguineous family, Liu et al. (2025) identified a homozygous deletion of the whole of exon 19 of the MEI1 gene. The deletion was found by whole-exome sequencing and confirmed by Sanger sequencing, and their mother was a heterozygous carrier. Sequencing of cDNA confirmed loss of exon 19, and exon 19 expression was almost undetectable in the patients. In transfected HEK293T cells, the deletion produced a truncated MEI1 protein, consistent with predicted premature termination in exon 20.

checks.explanation: Directly stated.
